tldr: Doc2Harness opened the thread on Oct 14 by measuring how much the harness around a model, not just the model, drives long-horizon coding-agent results. Papers then added search-state learning (ClueFlow), error-recovery tests for computer-use agents (CUA-Recovery) and a continual-learning exam.
whats_new: CALM (Oct 28) proposes conflict-aware lifecycle memory governance, so agents can retire outdated memories without losing the ability to reconstruct the past.
why_it_matters: Long-horizon agent failures come from harness design, silent state corruption, weak credit assignment and stale memory, so benchmarks that isolate those factors beat single-score leaderboards for platform decisions.

status.detail: Seven arXiv preprints, no independent replication yet; benchmarks, training methods and memory management are arriving together.

beats.headline: Doc2Harness benchmarks harness engineering for coding agents
Search state and computer-use error recovery get their own tests
Continual learning, web-search evaluation and critic training extend the focus
CALM adds lifecycle governance for agent memory

open_questions: Does any of these benchmarks get adopted by a major lab or independent evaluator?
Do the reported FOCUS gains hold on a third-party long-horizon benchmark?
Will CUA-Recovery results show shipped computer-use agents detecting silent state corruption?
Is CALM's memory governance evaluated on any of the existing long-horizon benchmarks?
take_for_builders: When evaluating a long-horizon agent, rerun it under your own harness and add an injected-error recovery case before trusting a leaderboard score; audit how your agent expires stale memory.
